def-holomorphic-kam-domain-and-diophanti:
## Definition

Throughout, fix an integer $n\ge1$. The space $\mathbb R^n$ is read through
[[rem-complex-euclidean-space-dictionary]] and $\mathbb C^n$ carries the polydisc
geometry of [[def-balls-and-polydiscs-in-complex-euclidean-space]]. All norms
below are supremum norms: for $z\in\mathbb C^m$,

$$|z|_\infty:=\max_{1\le i\le m}|z_i|,\qquad |z|_1:=\sum_{i=1}^m|z_i| .$$

**Angular torus.** Let $\mathbb Z$ be the integers ([[def-integers]]). Write
$k=(k_1,\dots,k_n)\in\mathbb Z^n$, $|k|_1=|k_1|+\dots+|k_n|$, and let
$(2\pi\mathbb Z)^n:=\{2\pi k:k\in\mathbb Z^n\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n$. On
$\mathbb R^n$ define the relation $\vartheta\sim\vartheta'$ by
$\vartheta-\vartheta'\in(2\pi\mathbb Z)^n$. This is an equivalence relation, and
the **angular torus** is the quotient set

$$\mathbb T^n:=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^n:=\mathbb R^n/\!\sim$$

with the quotient topology ([[def-quotient-topology]], [[def-product-topology]]),
and canonical projection $\pi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb T^n$, which is continuous
([[def-continuous-map-top]]). A map $f:\mathbb R^n\to X$ is **$2\pi$-periodic** if
$f(\vartheta+2\pi k)=f(\vartheta)$ for all $\vartheta\in\mathbb R^n$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^n$; such an $f$ factors uniquely through $\pi$, and a map on
$\mathbb T^n$ is, by definition, a $2\pi$-periodic map on $\mathbb R^n$ read
through this factorisation. A function on $\mathbb T^n$ is **continuous**, resp.
**real analytic**, when its $2\pi$-periodic representative has that property.

**Action-angle neighbourhoods.** For $0<r$ and $0<s\le\infty$ put

$$B_r:=\{I\in\mathbb C^n:|I|_\infty<r\},\qquad S_s:=\{\vartheta\in\mathbb C^n:|\mathrm{Im}\,\vartheta|_\infty<s\},$$

and, for a set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ (always measurably or
topologically qualified in the uses below) and $h\ge0$,

$$O_h(\Omega):=\{\nu\in\mathbb C^n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\nu,\Omega)<h\}, \qquad \operatorname{dist}_\infty(\nu,\Omega):=\inf_{\omega\in\Omega}|\nu-\omega|_\infty .$$

For $\Omega=\varnothing$ the infimum is taken in the extended nonnegative reals with $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$, so $O_h(\varnothing)=\varnothing$ for every finite $h\ge0$. Supremum norms of functions on an empty domain are $0$ (the supremum in $[0,+\infty]$). Thus an empty Diophantine label set gives an empty parameter family; results quantified over its labels are vacuous, and positive-measure assertions require their separately stated hypotheses.

The **action-angle neighbourhood** of width $(r,s,h)$ over $\Omega$ is the open
product

$$D_{r,s,h}(\Omega):=B_r\times S_s\times O_h(\Omega)\subseteq\mathbb C^{2n}\times\mathbb C^n,$$

and $D_{r,s}(\Omega):=B_r\times S_s$. In the KAM construction the parameter set
is a **frequency label set** $\Omega_\alpha\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ (defined below)
and the relevant parameter neighbourhoods are $O_h(\Omega_\alpha)$; the
temperature of a step is measured by the three widths $r,s,h$ and an angular
margin $\sigma>0$.

**Holomorphic data and norms.** A function $g:D_{r,s,h}(\Omega)\to\mathbb C$
is **holomorphic on $D_{r,s,h}(\Omega)$** when it is continuous and separately
holomorphic in each of the $2n+n$ complex variables
([[def-separately-holomorphic-function]],
[[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]]); equivalently, by
[[thm-power-series-expansion-in-several-complex-variables]], it is given near
every point by an absolutely convergent power series in the $(I,\vartheta,\nu)$
variables. The **sup-norms** are

$$|g|_{r,s}:=|g|_{r,s,0}:=\sup_{D_{r,s}(\Omega)}|g|,\qquad |g|_{r,s,h}:=|g|_{r,s,h}(\Omega):=\sup_{D_{r,s,h}(\Omega)}|g|\in[0,+\infty].$$

Where no parameter occurs we write $g\in\mathcal H_{r,s}$ if $g$ is holomorphic
on $D_{r,s}(\Omega)$ for some fixed open $\Omega$ and $|g|_{r,s}<+\infty$; and
$g\in\mathcal H_{r,s,h}$ if $g$ is holomorphic on $D_{r,s,h}(\Omega)$ with
$|g|_{r,s,h}<+\infty$. Functions of $\vartheta$ alone are read through the
$2\pi$-periodicity of the $\vartheta$-variables, so that all integrals and
norms below are well defined on $\mathbb T^n$.

**Fourier coefficients, mean and cutoff.** Let $g\in\mathcal H_{r,s}$. For
$k\in\mathbb Z^n$ and $I\in B_r$ the **Fourier coefficient** is the iterated
Riemann integral

$$g_k(I):=\frac1{(2\pi)^n}\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\cdots\!\int_0^{2\pi} g(I,\vartheta)\,e^{-ik\cdot\vartheta}\,d\vartheta_n\cdots d\vartheta_1 ,$$

as in [[def-sections-and-iterated-riemann-integrals]]; by
[[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] it equals the multiple Riemann
integral over $[0,2\pi]^n$ and is independent of the order of integration. The
**angular mean** of $g$ is $[g]:=g_0$, so $[g](I)=\frac1{(2\pi)^n}\int_{[0,2\pi]^n}g(I,\vartheta)\,d\vartheta$;
$g$ is **zero-mean** if $[g]=0$ for every $I\in B_r$. For a real number $K\ge0$
the **Fourier cutoff** $T_Kg$ is the trigonometric polynomial

$$T_Kg(I,\vartheta):=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n,\ |k|_1\le K}g_k(I)\,e^{ik\cdot\vartheta}.$$

The sum is finite because $|k|_1\le K$ bounds each $|k_i|$ by $K$. For a
function $g$ of $(I,\vartheta,\nu)$ the same notations apply with the
$\nu$-variable carried along; e.g. $[g]$, $g_k$ and $T_Kg$ are then functions of
$(I,\nu)$.

**Frequency label sets.** Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $\alpha>0$
and $\tau>n-1$. A frequency $\nu\in\mathbb R^n$ is **$(\alpha,\tau)$-Diophantine**
if

$$|k\cdot\nu|\ge\alpha\,|k|_1^{-\tau}\qquad\text{for every }k\in\mathbb Z^n\setminus\{0\},$$

with $k\cdot\nu=\sum_ik_i\nu_i$. The **label set** is

$$\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}:=\Omega\cap\{\nu\in\mathbb R^n:\nu\text{ is }(\alpha,\tau)\text{-Diophantine}\}.$$

$\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$ is closed in $\Omega$ and contained in the global
$(\alpha,\tau)$-Diophantine set; it need not have interior points. Write
$\widehat\Omega:=\Omega$ when $\tau,\alpha$ are fixed and no confusion arises.
The parameter neighbourhoods used below are $O_h(\Omega_{\alpha,\tau})$.

**Hamiltonians, canonical form and Poisson bracket.** A **Hamiltonian datum**
on $D_{r,s,h}(\Omega)$ is a holomorphic $H:D_{r,s,h}(\Omega)\to\mathbb C$ which
is real-valued on real points; more generally we consider families
$H(I,\vartheta;\nu)=e(\nu)+\nu\cdot I+P(I,\vartheta,\nu)$ where $e$ is
holomorphic on $O_h(\Omega)$ and real on real points, and
$P\in\mathcal H_{r,s,h}$ is real on real points. Pair the coordinates as
$q=\vartheta$, $p=I$ in the phase-domain notation of
[[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]]; the **standard
two-form** in these coordinates is

$$\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n d\vartheta_i\wedge dI_i,$$

and the **Hamiltonian vector field** of a $C^1$ Hamiltonian $H$ is, by
[[prop-cm-hamiltonian-field-and-poisson-bracket-in-a-phase-chart]] with
$(q,p)=(\vartheta,I)$,

$$X_H=(H_I,-H_\vartheta),\qquad \theta'=H_I,\quad I'=-H_\vartheta\ \ \text{(Hamilton's equations)},$$

characterised by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$; the **Poisson bracket** is

$$\{f,g\}=f_\vartheta\cdot g_I-f_I\cdot g_\vartheta,\qquad \{f,g\}=\nabla f^{\mathsf T}J\nabla g\ \ \text{in the notation of that item}.$$

In particular $\{f,e+\nu\cdot I\}=\nu\cdot f_\vartheta$ for every
$C^1$ function $f$.

**Angular parametrisations and Lagrangian images.** Fix a Hamiltonian datum
$H$. An **angular parametrisation** is a map $\psi=(\psi_I,\psi_\vartheta)$
with $\psi_I:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C^n$ $2\pi$-periodic and
$\psi_\vartheta:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C^n$ satisfying
$\psi_\vartheta(\vartheta+2\pi k)=\psi_\vartheta(\vartheta)+2\pi k$ for all
$k\in\mathbb Z^n$, so that
$\pi\circ\psi_\vartheta=\pi\circ(\psi_\vartheta\big|_{\mathbb R^n})$ descends to
$\mathbb T^n$; it is **holomorphic on the strip $S_s$** when both components
extend holomorphically to $S_s$, and **real analytic** when in addition
$\psi(\mathbb R^n)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ and the components are real analytic
in the real variables. It is **faithful** if
$\psi(\vartheta)=\psi(\vartheta')$ implies
$\vartheta-\vartheta'\in(2\pi\mathbb Z)^n$, and an **immersion** if
$D\psi(\vartheta)$ has rank $n$ for every $\vartheta\in\mathbb R^n$; a tuple
that is both is an **embedded torus parametrisation**. Its image is
**Lagrangian** (with respect to $\omega$) if
$\psi^*\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n d(\psi_\vartheta)_i\wedge d(\psi_I)_i=0$ as a
two-form on the parameter space of the representative, and **invariant with
frequency $\nu$** if

$$X_H(\psi(\vartheta))=\sum_{j=1}^n\nu_j\,\partial_{\vartheta_j}\psi(\vartheta) \qquad\text{for all real }\vartheta .$$
lem-cauchy-fourier-and-lattice-shell-bou:
## Statement

Fix $n\ge1$, $r>0$, $s>0$, $h\ge0$ and a set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$; write
$D_{r,s,h}:=D_{r,s,h}(\Omega)$ and let $g$ be holomorphic on $D_{r,s,h}$ with
finite norm $M:=|g|_{r,s,h}\in[0,\infty)$ ([[def-holomorphic-kam-domain-and-diophantine-labels]]).
Then:

1. **Fourier decay and representation.** For every $0<\sigma\le s$ the Fourier
   coefficients of $g$ satisfy
$$|g_k(I,\nu)|\le M\,e^{-(s-\sigma)|k|_1}\qquad(I\in B_r,\ \nu\in O_h,\ k\in\mathbb Z^n),$$
   and for $0<\sigma\le\min(s/2,1)$ the series
   $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}g_k(I,\nu)e^{ik\cdot\vartheta}$ converges absolutely
   and uniformly on $B_r\times S_{s-2\sigma}\times O_h$ to $g$; moreover each
   $g_k$ is holomorphic on $B_r\times O_h$, and the series can be differentiated
   termwise:
$$\partial_{\vartheta_j}g=\sum_kg_k\,ik_j\,e^{ik\cdot\vartheta},\qquad \partial_{I_j}g=\sum_k(\partial_{I_j}g_k)\,e^{ik\cdot\vartheta},\qquad \partial_{\nu_j}g=\sum_k(\partial_{\nu_j}g_k)\,e^{ik\cdot\vartheta}$$
   on $B_r\times S_{s-2\sigma}\times O_h$ (the last only when $h>0$), with absolute
   and uniform convergence of the differentiated series there.

2. **Cauchy bounds for the first and second derivatives.** For all $j$,
$$|\partial_{I_j}g|_{r-\delta,s,h}\le\frac{M}{\delta}\ (0<\delta<r),\qquad |\partial_{\vartheta_j}g|_{r,s-\delta',h}\le\frac{M}{\delta'}\ (0<\delta'<s),$$
$$|\partial_{\nu_j}g|_{r,s,h-\delta''}\le\frac{M}{\delta''}\ (0<\delta''<h),\qquad |\partial_{I_i}\partial_{I_j}g|_{r-\delta,s,h}\le\frac{2M}{\delta^2},\qquad |\partial_{\vartheta_i}\partial_{\vartheta_j}g|_{r,s-\delta',h}\le\frac{2M}{\delta'^2},\qquad |\partial_{I_i}\partial_{\vartheta_j}g|_{r-\delta,s-\delta',h}\le\frac{2M}{\delta\delta'}$$
   for all $i,j$ (the second-order bounds stated only for the ranges in which the
   norms on the left are defined).

3. **Lattice shells.** For every integer $m\ge1$,
$$\#\{k\in\mathbb Z^n:|k|_1=m\}\le 4^{\,n}m^{\,n-1},$$
   and for every $0<\sigma\le1$ the following finite sums satisfy
$$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}e^{-\sigma|k|_1}\le C_n\sigma^{-n},\qquad \sum_{k\ne0}|k|_1^{\,\tau}e^{-\sigma|k|_1}\le C_{n,\tau}\,\sigma^{-(\tau+n)}\quad(\tau\ge0),$$
$$\sum_{k\ne0}|k|_1^{-\tau}e^{-\sigma|k|_1}\le C_n\,\sigma^{-1}\quad(\tau\ge n-1),$$
   where $C_n$, $C_{n,\tau}$ depend only on the indicated arguments.

4. **Fourier truncation.** For $K\ge0$ and $0<\sigma\le\min(s/2,1)$,
$$|g-T_Kg|_{r,s-2\sigma,h}\le C_n\sigma^{-n}e^{-\sigma K}M .$$

5. **Algebra and uniform limits.** If $u,v$ are holomorphic and bounded on
   $D_{r,s,h}$ then $uv$ is holomorphic with $|uv|_{r,s,h}\le|u|_{r,s,h}|v|_{r,s,h}$;
   and if $(g^{(m)})$ is a sequence of holomorphic functions on $D_{r,s,h}$
   converging uniformly to $g$ on $D_{r,s,h}$ with $|g^{(m)}|_{r,s,h}\le M$ for all
   $m$, then $g$ is holomorphic on $D_{r,s,h}$ and $|g|_{r,s,h}\le M$.
lem-truncated-homological-equation-with-:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, $\tau>n-1$, $\alpha>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ carry its
$(\alpha,\tau)$-label set $\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$
([[def-holomorphic-kam-domain-and-diophantine-labels]]), and let $r>0$, $s>0$,
$K\ge0$ and $h\ge0$. Suppose one of the following two hypotheses holds, always with $2\pi$-periodicity in the angular variables and zero angular mean:

- **(G) general case:** $h=0$. For each fixed real $\nu\in\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$, the function $v(\cdot,\cdot,\nu)$ is holomorphic on $B_r\times S_s$, with a finite uniform bound $N:=\sup_{\nu,I,\vartheta}|v(I,\vartheta,\nu)|$. This is a parameter-free convention local to this item: the phase domain is $B_r\times S_s$ at that fixed real label, and no holomorphy in a nonopen real parameter set is asserted.
- **(T) truncated case:** $v$ is jointly holomorphic on $D_{r,s,h}(\Omega_{\alpha,\tau})$ with finite norm $N:=|v|_{r,s,h}$, and $v_k=0$ for $|k|_1>K$. For $K>0$, assume $h\le\alpha/(2K^{\tau+1})$. If $K=0$, the zero-mean datum is identically zero and no divisor restriction on $h$ is needed.

Then there is a constant $\alpha_0\ge\alpha/2$ (namely $\alpha_0=\alpha$ in case
(G) and $\alpha_0=\alpha/2$ in case (T)) such that
$|k\cdot\nu|\ge\alpha_0|k|_1^{-\tau}$ for every parameter in the specified case (real $\nu\in\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$ in (G), complex $\nu\in O_h(\Omega_{\alpha,\tau})$ in (T)) and every $k$ in the Fourier support of $v$, and:

1. **Existence, uniqueness and the equation.** For nonzero $k$, define $a_k:=v_k/(ik\cdot\nu)$ in (G), and for $0<|k|_1\le K$ in (T); set $a_k:=0$ for $|k|_1>K$ in (T). Thus discarded divisors are never used. The series
$$u(I,\vartheta,\nu):=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n,\,k\ne0}a_k(I,\nu)e^{ik\cdot\vartheta}$$
   converges absolutely and uniformly on $B_r\times S_{s-2\sigma}$ for every fixed real case-(G) label, and on $D_{r,s-2\sigma,h}(\Omega_{\alpha,\tau})$ in (T), whenever $0<\sigma\le1$ and $2\sigma<s$. Its sum is phase-holomorphic in (G), jointly holomorphic in (T), periodic and zero-mean, and satisfies $\nu\cdot\partial_\vartheta u=v$. Any two periodic holomorphic zero-mean solutions on a common such case domain agree there.
2. **Bounds.** For every $0<\sigma\le1$ with $4\sigma<s$, every $i,j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and every $0<\delta<r$:
$$|u|_{r,s-2\sigma,h}\le\frac{C_{n,\tau}}{\alpha_0}\sigma^{-(\tau+n)}N,\qquad |\partial_{\vartheta_j}u|_{r,s-3\sigma,h}\le\frac{C_{n,\tau}}{\alpha_0}\sigma^{-(\tau+n+1)}N,$$
$$|\partial_{I_j}u|_{r-\delta,s-2\sigma,h}\le\frac{C_{n,\tau}}{\alpha_0\,\delta}\sigma^{-(\tau+n)}N,\qquad |\partial_{\vartheta_i}\partial_{\vartheta_j}u|_{r,s-4\sigma,h}\le\frac{C_{n,\tau}}{\alpha_0}\sigma^{-(\tau+n+2)}N,$$
$$|\partial_{\vartheta_i}\partial_{I_j}u|_{r-\delta,s-3\sigma,h}\le\frac{C_{n,\tau}}{\alpha_0\,\delta}\sigma^{-(\tau+n+1)}N,\qquad |\partial_{I_i}\partial_{I_j}u|_{r-\delta,s-2\sigma,h}\le\frac{C_{n,\tau}}{\alpha_0\,\delta^2}\sigma^{-(\tau+n)}N .$$
3. **Truncation.** In case (T), the solution $u$ has $u_k=0$ for $|k|_1>K$;
   in particular $u$ and its derivatives displayed in clause 2 have the same
   Fourier support as $v$.
lem-kam-affine-taylor-fourier-truncation:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, $r>0$, $s>0$, $h>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, let
$K\ge0$, $0<\eta\le1/4$, $0<\sigma\le\min(1,s/4)$, and let $P$ be holomorphic
on $D_{r,s,h}(\Omega)$ with $|P|_{r,s,h}\le\varepsilon$
([[def-holomorphic-kam-domain-and-diophantine-labels]]). Define the **affine
action-Taylor polynomial**

$$Q(I,\vartheta,\nu):=P(0,\vartheta,\nu)+\sum_{j=1}^n \partial_{I_j}P(0,\vartheta,\nu)\,I_j ,$$

and the **truncated perturbation** $R:=T_KQ$ (Fourier cutoff in $\vartheta$).
Then:

1. **Taylor remainder.** $|P-Q|_{2\eta r,s,h}\le C\eta^2\varepsilon$ with a
   constant $C=C(n)$.
2. **Affine structure.** $Q$ and $R$ are holomorphic on $D_{r,s,h}(\Omega)$ and
   affine in $I$: $R(I,\vartheta,\nu)=R_0(\vartheta,\nu)+\sum_{j=1}^nR_j(\vartheta,\nu)I_j$
   with $R_0,R_j$ trigonometric polynomials in $\vartheta$ of degree at most
   $K$; $[R]=[Q]$ is affine in $I$, and $R-[R]$ is zero-mean.
3. **Size bounds.** $|Q|_{r,s,h}\le(n+1)\varepsilon$ and
$$|R|_{r,s-2\sigma,h}\le C_n\sigma^{-n}\varepsilon,\qquad \max_j|R_j|_{r,s-2\sigma,h}\le C_n\sigma^{-n}\varepsilon/r,\qquad |\partial_{\vartheta_i}R|_{r,s-2\sigma,h}\le C_n\sigma^{-n-1}\varepsilon .$$
4. **Truncation error.** $|Q-R|_{r,s-2\sigma,h}\le C_n\sigma^{-n}e^{-\sigma K/2}\varepsilon$.
lem-kam-generator-flow-and-remainder-bou:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, $\tau>n-1$, $\alpha>0$, and let $\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$ be the label set of [[def-holomorphic-kam-domain-and-diophantine-labels]]. Put $\mu:=\tau+3n+2$. Suppose $0<r\le1$, $s,h>0$, $K\ge1$, $0<\sigma\le1$, $8\sigma<s$, $0<\eta\le1/8$, and

$$h\le\frac{\alpha}{2K^{\tau+1}},\qquad K\sigma\ge1,\qquad \eta\le\sigma .$$

Let $P$ be holomorphic and $2\pi$-periodic in the angles on $D_{r,s,h}(\Omega_{\alpha,\tau})$, real-valued on real points, with $|P|_{r,s,h}\le\varepsilon$. Set

$$E:=\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha r\sigma^\mu},\qquad E\le c\eta,$$

where $c=c(n,\tau)>0$ is sufficiently small. All constants $C$ below depend only on $n,\tau$. Define the affine Taylor polynomial $Q$ and $R=T_KQ$ by [[lem-kam-affine-taylor-fourier-truncation]], and put $\widehat R=[R]$, $N=\nu\cdot I$. Let $F$ be the zero-mean solution, with Fourier support $|k|_1\le K$, of

$$\nu\cdot\partial_\vartheta F=R-\widehat R$$

from [[lem-truncated-homological-equation-with-conservative-loss]]. Order phase coordinates as $(I,\vartheta)$, so $X_F=(-F_\vartheta,F_I)$, $\omega=\sum_i d\vartheta_i\wedge dI_i$, and $\{f,g\}=f_\vartheta\cdot g_I-f_I\cdot g_\vartheta$. Put $W=\operatorname{diag}(r^{-1}I_n,\sigma^{-1}I_n)$. Then:

1. **Generator.** $F$ is holomorphic on $D_{r,s-2\sigma,h}$, affine in $I$, and $F_I$ is independent of $I$. It satisfies $\{F,N\}+\widehat R=R$ and
$$r^{-1}|F_\vartheta|_{3r/4,s-6\sigma,h}+\sigma^{-1}|F_I|_{3r/4,s-6\sigma,h}\le CE\sigma^{n+1},\qquad |W(DX_F)W^{-1}|_{3r/4,s-6\sigma,h}\le CE\sigma^{n+1}.$$
2. **Flow.** For $0\le t\le1$, the flow $\Phi_t$ is defined and holomorphic on $D_{r/2,s-8\sigma,h}$, with
$$\Phi_t:D_{r/2,s-8\sigma,h}\longrightarrow D_{3r/4,s-7\sigma,h}.$$
Here parameters are held fixed; $D\Phi_t$ denotes the derivative in $(I,\vartheta)$. The map is affine in $I$, its angle component is independent of $I$, and it obeys $\Phi_t(I,\vartheta+2\pi k,\nu)=\Phi_t(I,\vartheta,\nu)+(0,2\pi k)$. It is canonical, and real on real points. Uniformly in $t$,
$$|W(\Phi_t-\mathrm{id})|_{r/2,s-8\sigma,h}\le CE,\qquad |W(D\Phi_t-\mathrm{id})W^{-1}|_{r/2,s-8\sigma,h}\le CE,$$
$$h|W\partial_{\nu_j}\Phi_t|_{r/2,s-8\sigma,h/2}\le CE\qquad(1\le j\le n).$$
In addition, the small action domain has the inclusion
$$\Phi_t(D_{\eta r,s-8\sigma,h})\subseteq D_{2\eta r,s-7\sigma,h}.$$
3. **Remainder.** For $\Phi=\Phi_1$ and $\chi_t=(1-t)\widehat R+tR$, the identity
$$(N+P)\circ\Phi=N+\widehat R+P_+,\qquad P_+=(P-R)\circ\Phi+\int_0^1\{\chi_t,F\}\circ\Phi_t\,dt$$
holds on $D_{r/2,s-8\sigma,h}$, and on the smaller action domain
$$|P_+|_{\eta r,s-8\sigma,h}\le C\bigl[E+\eta^2+\sigma^{-n}e^{-\sigma K/2}\bigr]\varepsilon .$$
4. **Frequency shift.** Write $\widehat R(I,\nu)=a(\nu)+v(\nu)\cdot I$. Then $v$ is holomorphic on $O_h(\Omega_{\alpha,\tau})$, real on real points, and
$$|v|_{O_h}\le B:=C\frac{\varepsilon}{r}=C\alpha E\sigma^\mu,\qquad |Dv|_{O_{h/2}}\le\frac{2nB}{h}.$$

lem-kam-composed-map-and-derivative-conv:
## Statement

Use the sequences and hypotheses of [[lem-kam-parameter-sequences-satisfy-all-step-hypotheses]], with $n\ge2$, $\mu=	au+3n+2$, $\sigma_0\le s_0/32$, $h_j=h_04^{-\mu j}$ and $E_j\le E_04^{-(\mu+1)j}$. The step constants may be enlarged and their smallness constant decreased, depending only on $n,	au$. Put $\Lambda:=\Omega_{\alpha,	au}$ and $W_j:=\operatorname{diag}(r_j^{-1}I_n,\sigma_j^{-1}I_n)$.

Let $H_0(z,
u)=e_0(
u)+
u\cdot I+P_0(z,
u)$ be holomorphic and real on real points on $D_{r_0,s_0,h_0}(\Lambda)$, with $|P_0|\le\varepsilon_0$. Suppose at every stage the cited one-step suppliers produce the following data:

2. 3. The exact transformed identity
$$H_j(\widetilde\Phi_j(z,\phi_j(
u)),\phi_j(
u))=e_{j+1}(
u)+
u\cdot I+P_{j+1}(z,

Define the **extended** step and composition by

thm-parameter-kam-torus-invariance-and-l:
## Statement

Assume all the data, constants and hypotheses of
[[lem-kam-composed-map-and-derivative-convergence]] (in particular the sequences
of [[lem-kam-parameter-sequences-satisfy-all-step-hypotheses]], the initial
perturbation $P_0$ with $|P_0|\le\varepsilon_0$ and the one-step construction at
every stage), and assume in addition that the fixed data satisfy
$CE_0\le1/16$, where $C$ bounds both the composition constant $A$ and the one-step constant of
[[lem-kam-generator-flow-and-remainder-bound]] (a smallness condition on the
constants, available in the applications by shrinking the step constant). Let
$\Psi_\infty$ be the limiting family of
[[lem-kam-composed-map-and-derivative-convergence]], let
$$H(I,\vartheta,\nu):=e(\nu)+\nu\cdot I+P_0(I,\vartheta,\nu)$$
be the parameter Hamiltonian whose perturbing term is $P_0$, and let
$\omega=\sum_{i=1}^nd\vartheta_i\wedge dI_i$. Then for every
$\nu\in\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$:

1. **Invariance.** For every real $\vartheta$ in the strip,
$$X_H\bigl(\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta,\nu);\chi_\infty(\nu)\bigr) =\sum_{j=1}^n\nu_j\,\partial_{\vartheta_j}\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta,\nu),$$
   and the identity extends to the complex strip
   $|\mathrm{Im}\,\vartheta|_\infty<s_0/4$ by holomorphy of both sides.
   Here the second argument of $X_H$ records the original family parameter after all frequency retractions; the desired rotation frequency remains the target label $\nu$.
2. **Quasi-periodic motion.** For every $\vartheta_0\in\mathbb R^n$ the curve
   $s\mapsto\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta_0+s\nu,\nu)$ is an integral curve of the
   autonomous vector field $X_H(\,\cdot\,;\chi_\infty(\nu))$ wherever it is defined; that is,
$$\frac{d}{ds}\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta_0+s\nu,\nu) =X_H\bigl(\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta_0+s\nu,\nu);\chi_\infty(\nu)\bigr).$$
3. **Lagrangian images.** For every $\nu$ the pullback of $\omega$ along the
   real slice of $\vartheta\mapsto\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta,\nu)$ vanishes:
$$\Psi_\infty(\,\cdot\,,\nu)^*\omega=0\qquad\text{on the real slice, i.e.}\qquad \sum_{i=1}^nd(\Psi_\infty)_i^\vartheta\wedge d(\Psi_\infty)_i^I=0 .$$
lem-kam-limit-is-an-embedding:
## Statement

Assume the data, constants, sequences, one-step construction and notation of
[[lem-kam-composed-map-and-derivative-convergence]], the conjugacy symmetry of
[[lem-kam-conjugation-symmetry-of-the-construction]] (so that the initial
perturbation is conjugation-symmetric), and assume in addition that the fixed
data satisfy
$$4nCE_0\le1,$$
where $C$ bounds both the one-step constant and the composition constant $A$; this is a smallness condition on the fixed
constants, available in the applications by shrinking the step constant. Let
$\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta,\nu)=(b(\vartheta,\nu),\vartheta+w(\vartheta,\nu))$ be
the limiting family of [[lem-kam-composed-map-and-derivative-convergence]] and
$\Theta_\nu(\vartheta):=\vartheta+w(\vartheta,\nu)$ its angle component. Then for
every $\nu\in\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$:

1. **Contraction and injectivity.** For all real $\vartheta,\vartheta'$,
$$|w(\vartheta,\nu)-w(\vartheta',\nu)|_1\le\tfrac12|\vartheta-\vartheta'|_1,\qquad |\Theta_\nu(\vartheta)-\Theta_\nu(\vartheta')|_1\ge\tfrac12|\vartheta-\vartheta'|_1;$$
   in particular $\Theta_\nu$ is injective on $\mathbb R^n$ and
   $\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta,\nu)=\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta',\nu)$ with real
   $\vartheta,\vartheta'$ forces $\vartheta=\vartheta'$.
2. **Descent to the torus.** $\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta+2\pi k,\nu)=\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta,\nu)+(0,2\pi k)$ for every $k\in\mathbb Z^n$; consequently the parametrisation induces a well-defined continuous injective map
$$\widehat\Psi_\nu:\mathbb T^n\longrightarrow\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb T^n,\qquad \widehat\Psi_\nu\circ\pi=\Pi\circ\Psi_\infty(0,\,\cdot\,,\nu),$$
   where $\pi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb T^n$ is the quotient map and $\Pi$ reads the angle coordinates modulo $2\pi$.
3. **Immersion.** At every real $\vartheta$ the differential $D_\vartheta\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta,\nu)$ has rank $n$; equivalently $I_n+\partial_\vartheta w(\vartheta,\nu)$ is invertible.
4. **Embedding with Lipschitz inverse.** With $d_{\mathbb T^n}$ the quotient distance $d_{\mathbb T^n}(\pi\vartheta,\pi\vartheta'):=\min_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}|\vartheta-\vartheta'-2\pi k|_\infty$ and the supremum distance on $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb T^n$, the inverse of $\widehat\Psi_\nu$ on its image is Lipschitz with constant $2n$, and $\widehat\Psi_\nu$ is a homeomorphism of $\mathbb T^n$ onto its image; in particular the image is an embedded $n$-dimensional torus in the phase space, and it is real (clause 3 of [[lem-kam-conjugation-symmetry-of-the-construction]]).
5. **Dynamical reading.** The image of $\widehat\Psi_\nu$ is invariant under $X_H(\,\cdot\,;\chi_\infty(\nu))$ with frequency $\nu$ and Lagrangian, in the sense of clauses 1-3 of [[thm-parameter-kam-torus-invariance-and-lagrangianity]].
lem-nondegenerate-frequency-reduction-an:
## Statement

Let $n\ge2$, $\tau>n-1$, $\mu:=\tau+3n+2$, $\alpha>0$, $s_0>0$,
$0<\sigma_0\le\min(1,s_0/24)$, and let $c_1\in(0,1]$ be the one-step smallness
constant (the constant $c$ of the estimates of
[[lem-kam-generator-flow-and-remainder-bound]]). Let the following
data be given.

1. An open set $U\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, a compact set $K\subseteq U\cap\mathbb R^n$, a radius $0<r_0\le1$ with $\{J\in\mathbb C^n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(J,K)<2r_0\}\subseteq U$, a nonempty set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and a conjugation-invariant open complex neighbourhood $\Omega'\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ containing $\Omega$; and a holomorphic map $b:\Omega'\to U$ with $Dh(b(\nu))=\nu$ for every $\nu\in\Omega'$, where $h:U\to\mathbb C$ is holomorphic and $b(\Omega)+(B_{r_0}\cap\mathbb R^n)\subseteq K$. (In the applications $b=(Dh)^{-1}$ on a regular frequency patch, supplied by the real analytic inverse function theorem; here it is part of the data.)
2. A constant $M_2\ge1$ with $|I^{\mathsf T}D^2h(J)\,I|\le M_2|I|_\infty^2$ for all $I\in\mathbb C^n$ and all $J\in\{J':\operatorname{dist}_\infty(J',K)<2r_0\}$.
3. A holomorphic function $F$ on $\{J:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(J,K)<2r_0\}\times S_{s_0}$, $2\pi$-periodic in $\vartheta$, with $|F|\le\varepsilon$.

Put $r:=\sqrt{\varepsilon/M_2}$ and assume $0<r\le r_0$. Then:

1. **Taylor decomposition.** For every $\nu\in\Omega$ and $|I|_\infty\le r$,
$$h(b(\nu)+I)=h(b(\nu))+\nu\cdot I+P_h(I,\nu),\qquad |P_h(I,\nu)|\le M_2|I|_\infty^2 .$$
2. **Effective perturbation.** The function
$$G(I,\vartheta,\nu):=h(b(\nu)+I)-h(b(\nu))-\nu\cdot I+F(b(\nu)+I,\vartheta)$$
is holomorphic on $D_{r,s_0,h_0'}(\Omega)$ whenever $O_{h_0'}(\Omega)\subseteq\Omega'$ and $b(O_{h_0'}(\Omega))+B_r\subseteq\{J:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(J,K)<2r_0\}$, $2\pi$-periodic in $\vartheta$, and satisfies
$$|G|\le M_2r^2+\varepsilon=2\varepsilon .$$
3. **$\alpha^2$-smallness.** If
$$\varepsilon\le\frac{c_1^2}{4}\cdot\frac{\alpha^2\sigma_0^{2\mu}}{M_2},$$
then $|G|\le c_1\alpha r\sigma_0^{\mu}$; equivalently the relative smallness $E:=|G|/(\alpha r\sigma_0^{\mu})$ satisfies $E\le c_1$.
4. **Transfer to the physical Hamiltonian.** Let $H(p,\vartheta):=h(p)+F(p,\vartheta)$ and suppose that the parameter Hamiltonian
$$H_{\mathrm{par}}(I,\vartheta,\nu):=h(b(\nu))+\nu\cdot I+G(I,\vartheta,\nu)$$
satisfies the hypotheses of [[thm-parameter-kam-torus-invariance-and-lagrangianity]] on $D_{r,s_0,h_0'}(\Omega_{\alpha,\tau})$ (same sequences, same one-step construction, with $P_0:=G$), with limit phase family $\Phi_\infty=(\Phi_I,\Phi_\vartheta)$ and limit original-parameter map $\chi_\infty$. Then for every $\nu\in\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$ the physical family
$$\Psi_\nu(\vartheta):=\bigl(b(\chi_\infty(\nu))+\Phi_I(0,\vartheta,\nu),\ \Phi_\vartheta(0,\vartheta,\nu)\bigr)$$
satisfies
$$X_H\bigl(\Psi_\nu(\vartheta)\bigr)=\sum_{j=1}^n\nu_j\,\partial_{\vartheta_j}\Psi_\nu(\vartheta),\qquad \Psi_\nu^*\omega=0,$$
where $\omega=\sum_jd\vartheta_j\wedge dI_j$ and $X_H=(-H_\vartheta,H_I)$ is taken in the action-angle coordinates $(p,\vartheta)$; that is, the image is an invariant Lagrangian torus of the physical Hamiltonian $H$ with frequency $\nu$.
lem-diophantine-resonance-slab-measure:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, $\tau>n-1$, $\alpha>0$ and $R>0$, and write
$\ell(k):=|k|_1$ for $k\in\mathbb Z^n$ and $C_R:=(-R,R)^n$. For every nonzero
$k$ put
$$S_k:=\{\nu\in C_R:|k\cdot\nu|<\alpha\,\ell(k)^{-\tau}\},\qquad \mathcal R:=\bigcup_{k\in\mathbb Z^n\setminus\{0\}}S_k,$$
and let $D:=C_R\setminus\mathcal R$. Then:

1. **Slab bound.** For every $k\ne0$,
$$|S_k|\le 2^{n}n^{n/2}R^{n-1}\alpha\,\ell(k)^{-\tau-1}.$$
2. **Resonant set.** With $C_{n,\tau}:=2^{n}n^{n/2}4^{n}\sum_{m\ge1}m^{\,n-2-\tau}$ (a finite constant, since $\tau>n-1$),
$$|\mathcal R|\le C_{n,\tau}R^{n-1}\alpha .$$
3. **Diophantine set.** $D$ is measurable, is contained in the $(\alpha,\tau)$-Diophantine set
   $\{\nu\in C_R:|k\cdot\nu|\ge\alpha\ell(k)^{-\tau}\ \text{for all }k\ne0\}$, and
$$|D|\ge(2R)^n-C_{n,\tau}R^{n-1}\alpha ;$$
   consequently, for every $0<\alpha<\alpha_0(R,n,\tau):=(2R)^n/(C_{n,\tau}R^{n-1})$ the Diophantine set inside $C_R$ has positive measure.
4. **Boundary layer.** For every $0<\rho<R$ the same bounds hold with $R$ replaced by $R-\rho$, so the Diophantine set inside the closed cube $[-R+\rho,R-\rho]^n$ has measure at least $(2(R-\rho))^n-C_{n,\tau}(R-\rho)^{n-1}\alpha$; in particular frequencies at distance at least $\rho$ from the boundary of $C_R$ form a positive-measure Diophantine set once $\alpha$ is small enough.

All measures are $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure
([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]); the countable union
and the re-summation over shells use the standard countable bookkeeping
convention of [[def-countable-choice]], which is the only choice principle
involved.
thm-positive-measure-analytic-kam-family:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as required by the Lebesgue-measure frequency-set supplier. Let $n\ge2$, $\tau>n-1$, $\mu:=\tau+3n+2$, $s_0>0$ and
$0<\sigma_0\le\min(1,s_0/24)$. Let the following real analytic data be fixed.

1. An open set $U\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, a compact set $K\subseteq U\cap\mathbb R^n$, a radius $0<r_0\le1$ with $\{J\in\mathbb C^n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(J,K)<2r_0\}\subseteq U$, and a holomorphic, conjugation-symmetric function $h:U\to\mathbb C$ (so $h$ is real on the real points) with $h(K)\subseteq\mathbb R$.
2. A nonempty open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, a conjugation-invariant open complex neighbourhood $\Omega'\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ containing $\Omega$ and a holomorphic, conjugation-symmetric map $b:\Omega'\to U$ with $Dh(b(\nu))=\nu$ on $\Omega'$ and $b(\Omega)+(B_{r_0}\cap\mathbb R^n)\subseteq K$ (in the applications $b=(Dh)^{-1}$ on a regular frequency patch, supplied by [[thm-real-analytic-inverse-and-implicit-function-theorems]] when $\det D^2h\ne0$).
3. A constant $M_2\ge1$ with $|I^{\mathsf T}D^2h(J)I|\le M_2|I|_\infty^2$ for all $I\in\mathbb C^n$ and all $J\in U$ with $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(J,K)<2r_0$.
4. A holomorphic, conjugation-symmetric, $2\pi$-periodic in $\vartheta$ function $F$ on $\{J:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(J,K)<2r_0\}\times S_{s_0}$ with $|F|\le\varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon>0$ is the perturbation size of the statement, and a compact cube $C^*$ with positive side length and $\overline{C^*}\subseteq\Omega$ and $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\overline{C^*},\partial\Omega)>0$.

Then there exists a constant $c=c(n,\tau,s_0,\sigma_0,r_0,M_2,U,K,\Omega,h,b,C^*)>0$, and for every $0<\alpha$ with $\alpha<c$ and every perturbation size
$$0<\varepsilon\le c\,\alpha^2,$$
the following hold for the Hamiltonian $H(p,\vartheta):=h(p)+F(p,\vartheta)$ on the phase domain $U\cap\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb T^n$ with the two-form $\omega=\sum_jd\vartheta_j\wedge dI_j$:

1. **Positive-measure frequency set.** The set
$$\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}:=\{\nu\in\overline{C^*}:|k\cdot\nu|\ge\alpha|k|_1^{-\tau}\ \text{for all }k\in\mathbb Z^n\setminus\{0\}\}$$
   has positive Lebesgue measure, with $|\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}|\ge|\overline{C^*}|-C_{n,\tau}\,(\operatorname{diam}C^*)^{n-1}\alpha$ for the constant $C_{n,\tau}$ of [[lem-diophantine-resonance-slab-measure]].
2. **Invariant Lagrangian tori.** For every $\nu\in\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$ there is a continuous injective map
$$\widehat\Psi_\nu:\mathbb T^n\longrightarrow\bigl(U\cap\mathbb R^n\bigr)\times\mathbb T^n,\qquad \widehat\Psi_\nu\circ\pi=\Pi\circ\Psi_\infty(0,\,\cdot\,,\nu),$$
   which is a homeomorphism onto its image and satisfies
$$X_H\bigl(\widehat\Psi_\nu(\vartheta)\bigr)=\sum_{j=1}^n\nu_j\,\partial_{\vartheta_j}\widehat\Psi_\nu(\vartheta),\qquad \widehat\Psi_\nu^*\omega=0 ;$$
   the parametrisation is read in the lifts, and $\pi,\Pi$ are the quotient maps of the angle variables.
3. **Closeness and regularity.** Writing $\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta,\nu)=(b(\nu)+\Phi_I(0,\vartheta,\nu),\vartheta+w(\vartheta,\nu))$, one has the bounds $|\Phi_I(0,\vartheta,\nu)|\le2C_{\mathrm{phys}}rE_0$ and $|w(\vartheta,\nu)|\le2C_{\mathrm{phys}}\sigma_0E_0$ with $r=\sqrt{\varepsilon/M_2}$ and $E_0=2\sqrt{\varepsilon M_2}/(\alpha\sigma_0^{\mu})$, and the total action correction $\Phi_I$ includes the frequency-retraction change of its centre. Here $C_{\mathrm{phys}}$ is a fixed finite constant depending on the stated analytic data, including a bound for $Db$ near $C^*$. The family $\nu\mapsto\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta,\nu)$ is Lipschitz on $\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$ with a finite constant at most $C_{\mathrm{phys}}[1+(r+\sigma_0)E_0/h_0]$, where $h_0=\alpha/(2K_0^{\tau+1})$ is the initial frequency width chosen in the proof. The constant term retains the variation of the unperturbed centre $b(\nu)$.

No probability, frequency-of-occurrence or empirical claim is made; the
conclusion is a statement about the Lebesgue measure of a set of frequencies.
lem-kam-conjugation-symmetry-of-the-cons:
## Statement

Assume the data, constants, sequences, one-step construction and notation of
[[lem-kam-composed-map-and-derivative-convergence]], and assume that the initial
perturbation is **conjugation-symmetric**:
$$P_0(\bar I,\bar\vartheta,\bar\nu)=\overline{P_0(I,\vartheta,\nu)}\qquad\text{for every }(I,\vartheta,\nu)\in D_{r_0,s_0,h_0}(\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}).$$
For a holomorphic $g$ on a conjugation-invariant domain put
$g^c(I,\vartheta,\nu):=\overline{g(\bar I,\bar\vartheta,\bar\nu)}$, and call $g$
conjugation-symmetric when $g^c=g$. Then:

1. **One-step objects.** For every $j\ge0$ the functions $P_j$, $Q_j$, $R_j$,
   $\widehat R_j$, $F_j$ and $v_j=\partial_I\widehat R_j(0,\cdot)$ are
   conjugation-symmetric on their domains, and
   $\phi_j(\bar\nu)=\overline{\phi_j(\nu)}$; in particular $\phi_j$ maps real
   points to real points.
2. **The maps.** The extended steps $T_j(z,\nu)=(\widetilde\Phi_j(z,\phi_j(\nu)),\phi_j(\nu))$ and their compositions are conjugation-symmetric. In particular $\Psi_j^c=\Psi_j$ and $\chi_j^c=\chi_j$ for every $j$.
3. **The limit.** $\Psi_\infty^c=\Psi_\infty$ and $\chi_\infty^c=\chi_\infty$; in particular for real
   $\vartheta$ and real $\nu$ the point $\Psi_\infty(0,\vartheta,\nu)$ is real,
   that is $b(\vartheta,\nu)\in\mathbb R^n$ and $w(\vartheta,\nu)\in\mathbb R^n$.
